snapshot.title: UPSC History: Quit India Movement & INA
snapshot.exam_hook: 🏔️ UPSC History Hook: 1942: Quit India. Do or Die: Gandhi. Usha Mehta: Radio. Satara: Parallel Gov. Bose: INA/Jai Hind. 1946: RIN Mutiny.

quick_notes.title: Quit India (August 1942)
quick_notes.detail: "Vardha Resolution". Launched at Gowalia Tank, Bombay. Slogan : "Do or Die" (Karo ya Maro). Most leaders arrested on the first day (Operation Zero Hour).

quick_notes.title: Spontaneous Uprising
quick_notes.detail: Leaderless movement. Massive strikes, sabotage of rail lines, and telegraphs. Underground Radio : Started by Usha Mehta in Bombay.

quick_notes.title: Parallel Governments
quick_notes.detail: Nationalist govts formed in: 1. Ballia (Chittu Pandey). 2. Tamluk (Jatiya Sarkar). 3. Satara (Prati Sarkar - longest running).

quick_notes.title: Subhas Chandra Bose & INA
quick_notes.detail: Left INC (Tripuri Crisis 1939), formed Forward Bloc. Escaped to Germany/Japan. Took over Azad Hind Fauj (founded by Mohan Singh/Rash Behari Bose). Slogan : "Jai Hind", "Delhi Chalo".

quick_notes.title: Impact of INA
quick_notes.detail: INA Trials at Red Fort (1945) created a massive wave of sympathy. INC leaders (Nehru, Bhulabhai Desai) defended them. Led to the Royal Indian Navy (RIN) Revolt in 1946.

topic_title: UPSC History: Quit India Movement & INA
lesson_intro: Today we study the 'Final Blow'. The Quit India Movement (1942) was the most violent and spontaneous mass uprising since 1857. With the slogan 'Do or Die', Gandhi gave a clarion call for the British to leave immediately. Simultaneously, Subhas Chandra Bose led the Indian National Army (INA) from outside. For UPSC, focus on the 'Underground activities' of leaders like Usha Mehta and the significance of the 'Parallel Governments'. This is the endgame of the Raj.
